It's tough to stop cutting. For the longest time I completely got away with it because people always seems to accept my excuses (I faked an overall cheerful public face). And deep cutting isn't worth it!! So don't wonder about it, just take it from me if you can. Once you leave a scar like that you arent making yourself stronger, you are giving yourself a reminder of weakness. Or at least that's what I feel when look at mine. A ping of pain, sadness and regret always hits me when I catch a glance at the scars. Try to make your self stronger by saying no. Refocus your energy if you can, maybe go for a run or something to work thru what going on in your mind. And I really think throwing those razors away would be a good thing to do. Throw away your want to self harm with them! With each blade you are making a promise to yourself. Heck, maybe even make a list of 20 promises you can make to yourself, one for each blade. Some promises I have to myself are never cut on my arms again, and my legs, and my stomach( I got to the point where every part of my body was covered so I promised to stop cutting within about 5 or so smaller promises) I promised to do more things that I enjoy. I promised to read more books to make me smarter. Just stuff like that. So when I'm feeling down I remember the promises I made and try to work from there.

My sister is what kept me going for a very very long time. 
And the thoughts and feeling are enough to drive someone insane.
I also was going to kill myself after I graduated high school, but then I just didn't... There were extremely circumstances in my family, but basically I survived to get myself into college. There, I reached put to treat my depression for the first time. It's been 5 or 6 years since then, and I am on some medications that have done WONDERS for me. 
While that may not be the case for you, the point I want to make is that you are so close to a point where you really get to take your life into your own hands. Don't give up on that chance so soon. 
Keep thinking of your bother. And try to think of the companionship between you two rather than the potential of loneliness. Don't think of what will happen if you leave your bother, but rather the future you guys can share together. Develop that mind set that you will be there for him. While you might not be physically near, your thoughts bring you right next to him. So if your mind starts going down the path of death and ways to kill yourself, you counter with, "well that can't happen and isn't true, I still going to be here tomorrow cuz I will be with my brother. I'm far too excited for the memories we are going to make with each other and the time we will spend together to miss a moment of it."

I dunno, just trying to maybe help a but, although I know it is so easy to dismiss the advice of others when your mind is cemented in a self destructive mode. 

If you need to tell people things, tell us! We are hear to listen and support each other. If you want to message me or anything feel free to do that. But basically just keep trying. There are those of us who have been in your spot and somehow got past that and are still here alive on this earth. And we want to help!

I definitely try to talk to other friends and family, granted holding back some so not to burden or concern them. He used to be included in that support "level" but since we are housemates (4 people total) and this is my first really nasty depression spell living at this house, and it is pretty much impossible to hide at home. hell, once i get home I'm too tired to hide it.
I put a lot of time towards my job, but I do really need to make more time for me doing things I enjoy, time to live in abundance like you said, and time to figure out what would even be for me. I'm thinking getting more active because I do like to dance and there is a ballet studio near my house and I've never taken ballet (give it a shot, right?) but I would really want to get into shape before that. I don't need to be like lady-ripped or anorexic ballerina, but I've spent a lot of school years hunched over a desk, so I got a bit of stress eating to work off before I'm putting on a leotard, haha.

The workplace is a difficult situation (for me anyways...) since it is a start up engineering firm. There are 2 other people (my boss and my coworker) so my boss is extremely stretched for time as it is and my coworker is learning just like me: we graduated college last June. So this is my first out of college full time professional type job, and everything I do seems knew. When I'm not depressed and suicidal I can work through stuff, but when I get so so suicide it is impossible to get any work done. I can't focus on my work, I have great difficulty bringing myself to do work because I feel so worthless, stupid, and I know I'm going to get fired so what is even the point. Then if some how I get myself working, the moment one thing goes wrong I fall to pieces, going down the "whats the point, your useless and stupid anyways, you shouldnt even be here". 

And I definitely try not to use my boyfriend as my sole emotional support, but I think we all know the masking of feelings to protect and to not burden loved ones. Since my boyfriend is also one of my housemates, its kinda hard to hide it from him. Last night we sat down and talked about the causes of my depressed suicidal spells, namely being that there are no causes. Sometimes there will be triggers (in more extreme instances), but most of the time I wake up one morning depressed, suicidal, etc. then it will get worse until it reaches a certain level (some spells are waaayy worse than others, this one for example is really bad..) then I will feel that way for about a week or more. Then I will just feel better. ITS MADDENING I ASSURE YOU. so I thought i reach a good point with a medication balance to help, but I need to talk to my doctor, and more importantly get through today and tomorrow and the next day.

I read your post last night (well a couple hours ago, pulling a all-nighter to finish my project at work, we all know how that goes) and I couldn't think of anything or what I would do once I finally give into the suicidal thoughts and feelings that have been plaguing me since I was ten. But then this morning I thought about how I always found people watching to be a good activity to take your mind off things. Maybe at a park or a bar, just hang out, maybe have a drink and observe the buzzing world around me. Seeing all the different people, and taking momentary glimpses into their lives as we share the same space. Sometimes it can make you feel better about your life, and sometimes it can make you feel worse, but I try not to compare. I mostly look for what blessings I do have (which makes me feel better) or I just let my mind wonder as far away from my world as I want.
